phase: WS-1 of the flight-reliability program. Add a CRUISE stall-detector / no-freeze guard to the supercruise pilot + autopilot tour so the unattended Orrery screensaver can never freeze permanently. Root cause (flight-audit Phase 2/3): SupercruisePilot CRUISE has no timeout (only ALIGN does), so a leg whose straight path is blocked by the star (wedge), or that chases a moon orbiting too fast to catch (overshoot limit-cycle), or a tour stop with a null bodyRef, stays in CRUISE / never advances forever. Approach: (1) a rolling-window dist-not-decreasing detector INSIDE SupercruisePilot, active only in CRUISE, that aborts the leg after ~10-15s of no net progress; on abort a tour advances to the next stop (skip-and-continue), a standalone Assist leg drops out gracefully; (2) a null-bodyRef skip-guard on the tour-advance path; (3) a standing runFlightReliabilitySuite() built alongside. Default: a non-convergent fast-moon leg is SKIPPED (not captured) — capture via target-lead is deferred to WS-4. Out of scope: obstacle-avoidance/re-routing, SC_TUNING floor re-tuning, any change to warp / HELM manual / commitBurn / Toybox beyond the stall guard, new abort HUD.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The CRUISE stall-detector aborts a wedged leg. Given a leg pre-aligned into CRUISE whose straight ship->target line is blocked by the star (the antipodal star-wedge: dist pins at the collision barrier / forced-drop horizon, speed ~0, dist never decreasing), the pilot aborts the leg within the stall window + margin instead of staying in CRUISE forever. The abort is observable on the pilot (phase leaves CRUISE / an abort flag on the PilotFrame).

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest with real classes (fresh SupercruiseModel + SupercruisePilot, star radius 4.65, ship on the far side of the star from a real planet, orientation set toward target, beginLeg, then step pilot.update(dt)+model.setBodies([star,target])+model.update(dt) each frame). Mirror src/flight/__tests__/SupercruisePilot.align.test.js.
verifyVia.observable: Within stallWindow + a small margin the pilot signals abort (phase != CRUISE, e.g. IDLE, and/or frame.stallAborted true); before the window it stays in CRUISE; without the fix it would stay CRUISE for the whole run.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A leg that is genuinely still closing on its target is NEVER falsely aborted. Given a normal CRUISE approach whose dist is monotonically (or net) decreasing, the detector never fires and the leg proceeds to HOLD and motionComplete exactly as it does today.

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest: a clear-line leg (line offset from star >= 10u, or open space) stepped to completion; assert the detector never trips over a run longer than the stall window.
verifyVia.observable: phase progresses ALIGN->CRUISE->HOLD, motionComplete fires, and frame.stallAborted is never set; identical outcome to the pre-fix pilot on this input.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A deliberate Assist/commit-burn park (reaches HOLD and orbits with linger:Infinity) is never treated as a stall. Because the detector keys on CRUISE only, a leg sitting in HOLD indefinitely is left alone (no abort, no spurious advance).

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest: a leg that captures to HOLD with linger:Infinity, stepped well past the stall window.
verifyVia.observable: phase stays HOLD, the ship keeps orbiting, frame.stallAborted never set, motionComplete never forced by the detector.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A tour stop whose bodyRef is null is skipped and the tour continues to the next valid stop (or completes) rather than freezing with no leg. The advance logic re-advances past null-bodyRef stops.
